subject: FastPay SLO readout & autoscale plan — post-call
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastpay.com>, Lindsey Park <lindsey@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastPay SLO readout & autoscale plan — post-call

Hi Tom / Lindsey —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and I wanted to capture a short readout and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Call highlights (notes):
- Traffic shape: short bursts from transaction engine (~10–30s), sustained batch jobs overnight (~2–3 hours). Peak qps observed during business hours: ~550 qps for small payloads, occasional spikes to ~1.2k qps for ~15–30s.
- Targets you mentioned: p95 latency <= 350ms for non-streaming responses; streaming use cases need initial token latency < 250ms and steady-state per-token latency < 40ms.
- Concurrency expectations: typical concurrency ~30–60 active sessions, burst concurrency up to ~400 for front-facing endpoints.
- Availability/SLO ask: 99.95% with graceful degradation rather than hard failures during extreme spikes.

Immediate asks for Redwood to qualify:
1) Can we validate scale-up times from cold to target concurrency (30 -> 400) for FastPay workload?
2) Verify warm-pool sizing recommendations and priming windows for your traffic shape.
3) Streaming gap: ensure SDK keepalive behavior and continuous batching don't add >100ms to initial streaming token.
4) Confirm queueing/backpressure behavior under sustained >1k qps bursts (what we surface to the app).

Deliverables I’ll push next:
- A short test plan to validate scale-up times and warm-pool priming (I’ve attached a first-draft proposal).
- Mutual action plan with milestones for a two-week pilot and required FastPay inputs.

Please send the traffic sample you mentioned (CSV with timestamps + request payload size) — that will let us tailor the test and sizing.

Next steps / timeline:
- Tom: share CSV + expected busiest 3 windows by end of day tomorrow (10/05).
- Redwood (me + Marissa): produce a tailored autoscale test plan and proposal by 10/07.
- Align on pilot dates week of 10/18.

Attachment: Redwood_autoscale_proposal.pdf (draft)

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

--
Priya Natarajan
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastpay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Lindsey Park <lindsey@fastpay.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastPay SLO readout & autoscale plan — post-call

Priya —

Thanks for the summary — that matches what we walked through. I attached the traffic sample you requested (fastpay_traffic_samples.csv). A few clarifications from our end:

- The 1.2k qps spikes are typically very short (15–45s) and tied to batch-triggered push notifications across regions. The payload size for those spikes is usually 400–900 bytes.
- Streaming usage is concentrated on our customer-facing chat assistant (~5–7 concurrent per minute) but each session can stream for up to 60s. The strictest requirement is initial token latency — customers notice a >300ms delay.
- For the overnight batches, throughput is lower (~150 qps) but sustained which may affect cache/kv behavior.

Attachment: fastpay_traffic_samples.csv (CSV)

If you can include a simple ramp/soak test that simulates the 15–45s spikes, that would be ideal.

—Tom
Tom Nguyen
VP, Engineering | FastPay
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: FastPay SLO readout & autoscale plan — post-call

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding the FastPay thread and attached traffic sample. TL;DR and ask for engineering qualification: 

TL;DR: FastPay needs p95 <= 350ms for non-streaming, initial streaming token < 250ms, steady per-token < 40ms. Peak short spikes to ~1.2k qps (15–45s). Typical concurrency bursts up to ~400. They prefer graceful degradation over outright errors.

Primary asks for runtime team: 
- Can we run a targeted autoscale test that exercises: cold -> 400 concurrency ramp within a 60s wall time (simulate their short spikes)? Use their CSV as the request arrival pattern.
- Provide warm-pool sizing guidance: how many pre-warmed workers/instances to maintain to meet p95 target without relying on cold starts. Include priming window recommendation (how long to keep warm instances after idle).
- Streaming: validate SDK keepalive and continuous batching settings to meet initial token <250ms. If extra SDK changes needed, flag them.
- Queueing behavior: under sustained >1k qps, describe whether we will queue requests vs. shed and what HTTP codes/error messages app will receive; propose backpressure headers we can include.

Proposed quick approach: 
1) Test harness on Redwood staging using FastPay sample. 2) Run three scenarios: (A) 0->400 ramp within 60s, (B) repeated 15–45s spikes up to 1.2k qps, (C) overnight 2–3 hour sustained 150 qps with cache warm/cold variants. 3) Capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, token-level steady-state numbers, and scale-up timeline metrics.

Deliverable I want from you both by EOD 10/06: a short runbook (bullet list) for the harness and a recommended warm-pool configuration (counts + priming TTL). I’ll convert into the mutual_action_plan.xlsx we’ll share with FastPay.

Forwarded attachments: fastpay_traffic_samples.csv

Thanks —
Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FastPay SLO readout & autoscale plan — post-call

Priya —

Thanks for the forward and nice summary. Quick notes from the runtime side after a first pass through the CSV:

- Approach looks good: we can run the three scenarios you outlined in staging. I recommend starting with a conservative warm-pool of 40 pre-warmed workers for the pilot, with a primordial TTL of ~10 minutes (keep them alive for 10m after last use) — that should handle the 30–60 normal concurrency and blunt many of the short spikes.
- For the 0->400 ramp within 60s: we can meet the p95 <= 350ms target provided we use a hybrid of warm-pool + fast scale (GPU spin-up + model shard activation). I’ll detail expected scale-up timeline in the runbook (approx: 0–40 from warm pool <250ms, 40–200 scale step ~12–18s, 200–400 additional shards ~20–30s under staging network conditions).
- Streaming: SDK keepalive tuning + reduced continuous batching window should keep initial token <250ms in 90% of cases; we’ll capture distribution. If they need 99%+ for initial token <250ms we may need more aggressive pre-warming or region-level warm pools.
- Queueing/backpressure: for staging we’ll surface a 429 with a Retry-After header at sustained rates beyond our configured burst capacity; for graceful degradation we can enable token throttling with a soft-fail mode that returns partial results with a 207 multi-status (this is something to discuss with FastPay product).

I’ll produce the runbook and an initial set of test commands + infra config by EOD 10/06 and attach a short PDF summary for them.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
